note: Lesson 7.2 (solution design) has no workflow build: its solved problem is a signed design.

walk.title: Solve it: Kora's CRM design on paper first

steps.say: Requirements are signed. Now we design the CRM on paper, so the build is just following the plan.
Draw the model. Kora's plan includes custom objects, so Property becomes its own object, linked to contacts and deals.
show: No custom objects? Note it as a limitation

steps.say: Write the data dictionary: twenty-seven custom fields, every dropdown value listed, and the stage where each required field becomes required.
Four pipelines, each stage with an exit rule. Sales runs from new enquiry through viewing and offer to legal and payment.
show: Every stage has an exit rule

steps.say: Teams for Lekki sales, Ibadan sales and lettings. Commission and landlord bank details stay out of the CRM, and only the owner and admin can export.
New enquiries are shared round-robin among available agents whose area matches. Deals are named by property address and buyer surname.
show: Every deal: an owner and a next-step date

steps.say: A forty-five-minute walkthrough with two real deals. They spot one gap, short-lets, which goes into lettings with a deal type. Then they sign.

walk.end: That's the design: one model, one dictionary, clear pipelines and permissions, signed before anyone clicks Create.
